notes.title: 1.0.5 is live!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44950659/718cb772a3cc038c000627832e331303c2f25b36.png[/img]
Hi all! Nacho here.

Just a quick bugfixes pass.

Prior to this patch, if you were starting a new profile it would send you back to profile selection.  That had to do with a bug in which if you used profiles 2 or 3, once entering a name it'd still select profile 1 on the first time.

Whilst it wasn't gamebreaking as this is a roguelite, I still didn't want to ship that bug so had to resort to that annoying solution.

Now, no more.  That bug is gone.  It was so simple and so dumb that it took me AGES to find it.

Also, now the mouse cursor does pretty lights, yay.

That's it!

Thanks!

Nacho

notes.title: New Control Schemes! V1.0.4
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44950659/43afd6dee257827c58a13fdc6c4264e897b00c27.png[/img]

Hi all!  

As per feedback received, I've been very hard at work revising the control scheme for the game.  With the new control schemes it might feel a bit easy, so feel free to bump up the difficulty a bit.

I might add settings for a static control scheme if the dynamic one proves to be annoying, just needed to keep a scope!

Also, trying the game on my SteamDeck I realized how annoying it had to be to hunt down the on-screen keyboard, which could represent a softlock for some people.  Thanks to the GODOT community, I found a great solution to that problem.

[h3]Dynamic New Control Scheme![/h3]
[list]
[*] Traditional one-handed control scheme remains
[*] You can now use the mouse to aim, to play with mouse and keyboard.  If the mouse is left idle, it'll revert to the one-handed scheme in a few seconds
[*] You can now use the right stick of your controller to aim (twin stick shooter style).  Revert to mouse control by clicking
[/list]
[h3]Added[/h3]
[list]
[*] Reticle
[*] Onscreen Keyboard
[/list]
[h3]Changes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Revamped Pause System (less buggy)
[*] Revamped Range System for Ship Weapon
[*] Rebalanced Time Reversal Engine
[*] Pushing through Greed Stages will increase the stakes but you'll reach the point of diminishing returns... Figure it out
[/list]
[h3]Bugfixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Now if you lose by going negative time, it'll finish the game correctly
[*] Vortex despawning correctly on finished stage transition
[*] Some old bugs and lots of new bugs introduced along the way
[/list]
If you experience any bugs or anything, feel free to send me a message or post it in the Community hub (now that I know that exists, I'll be checking!)

As always, thank you so much!

Nacho

notes.title: V 1.0.3!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44950659/3c9f1558f32abdf94ea31d7fb59b53a8b54c013a.png[/img]

Hi there!   I've been working on some changes that are live now!

I've introduced Difficulty as an option that will affect how long you are likely to survive.  For balance purposes, the easier the game is, the less score you'll be earning.

[h2]Now, to the content![/h2]
If you read any introduction to Computer Science the first thing they tell you is what we all know as bugs are, in reality, mistakes.  

[h3]Mistakes fixed:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed Speed and Size Powerups
[*] Seeing the victory screen without actually winning the game
[*] You could softlock your run by going negative greed.  That won't happen anymore
[/list]
Delving into UI/UX, I've been dabbling into making many screens easier to work with.

[h3]QoL Changes:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added a Difficulty Settings screen accessible from the Start Menu
[*] Added Sound Volume sliders for you to customize how you want it to sound
[*] The Laser Sight is now a permanent option.  You take a hit in your score multiplier though
[*] Other QoL improvements, It looks nicer in general
[/list]
--------------------------------------------------------

As always, I welcome all feedback!  This is a passion project for me so anything new I can work into it, I'll do my best to.

Thanks!

Nacho

notes.title: Time Avarice goes V1.0.2!
notes.content:
[h2]Hey everyone![/h2]

First of all, [b]THANK YOU[/b] to all who purchased the game and/or wishlisted.  I'm very pleased with this accomplishment.

This is a quick patch addressing a few things:
[list]
[*]Changed how savefiles and config files are managed (see more below)
[*]Fixed a few bugs
[*]A notable bug was the ship rotation animation.  Now you'll see it rotate more smoothly rather than a snap
[*]Buffed the Ranged Weapon Systems for those who can't aim (including myself)
[/list]
[h3]IMPORTANT INFO ABOUT YOUR SAVEFILE![/h3]
Savefiles have moved! However your progress hasn't been lost (unless you were unfortunate to update with an error during a hotfix, which inspired me to fix this system once and for all, sorry!).

If you were already playing, you can 
[olist]
[*] Hunt down your old savefile at: C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\TimeAvarice\SaveFiles 
[*] Paste it in: C:\Users\youruser\AppData\Roaming\Time Avarice\SaveFiles (optionally you can always do Win + R and type in %appdata% to get there faster)
[/olist]
If you have any difficulties with that, I'm more than happy to help you troubleshoot.

Lastly, if you manage to "finish" the game, shoot me a screenshot and I'll feature it!

Thanks again for the support!

Nacho

Questions, comments, or stumbled upon a bug? Hit me up at timeavaricegame@outlook.com

notes.title: Time Avarice is NOW AVAILABLE!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44950659/ec67956e15823cb413ee8f93a4d83aebd153993a.png[/img]

[h1]HUZZA! [b]Time Avarice[/b] has ARRIVED![/h1]

[h2]Hey everyone![/h2]

I'm incredibly excited to announce that [b]Time Avarice[/b] is officially OUT NOW on [b]Steam[/b]!

This wouldn't have been possible without all of you – the playtesters, the supporters, and everyone who's been excited about this project. Thank you from the bottom of my heart!

The first impression you are likely to have is that the game is [i]too [/i]hard. This is intentional. You are limited to a maximum of 5 different powerup families per game, preventing you from becoming an all-powerful [i]Brilliant Behemoth[/i].  Discovering effective powerup synergies is part of the challenge, and I leave that part to you.

The game's complexity might lead you to discover unintended uses for mechanics.  I might have missed an exploit or two during development... or maybe not. See if you can find them, and put them to good use.  It's a single-player game after all.

Questions, comments, or stumbled upon a bug? Hit me up at timeavaricegame@outlook.com


Thanks again for the support, and I can't wait to see you all getting greedy and reaching higher scores!

Nacho

notes.title: 48 Hours to Time Avarice
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44950659/9f905a3af112ee385cf8b81764234f2ca0b0feeb.png[/img]

Hi again!

Once again, thank you to everyone who checked out the store and wish listed the game! 

[b]Time Avarice[/b] goes live in about 48 hours, so as promised, here are some quick insights to help you prepare for this [i]very [/i]punishing game.

There are only three main concepts to grasp to understand how Time Avarice works: 
[list]
    [*][b]Time:[/b] Your only resource. Spend it to buy PowerUps, and earn it mainly by destroying crystals and clearing stages. Run out of time, and it's a one-way trip to the Game Over screen
    [*][b]Greed:[/b] This affects many aspects of the game. For now, know that it influences difficulty and how much time you gain or lose. The greedier you are, the higher the risk and reward
    [*][b]Chrono Volatility:[/b] Time is unstable in Time Avarice. As Chrono Volatility increases, PowerUps become more expensive, and your gains or losses of time are amplified
[/list]
Remember:  There is no escape, just a higher score.

notes.title: Time Avarice releases April 11th!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44950659/0b8b3b3c8274e48829e3bc0d1d986faa75e6e404.png[/img]

Hi, I'm Nacho! First time I do one of these.

I'll start saying Thank You to all those who checked the store out and wish listed the game. This game has been a passion project of mine for some time.

Time Avarice started as a simple tech-demo to see how many things I could learn to program from scratch, mutated into a feature-creep chimera of all things I enjoy seeing in games I like and then turned into a simple gameplay loop that makes it its own thing.

Prior to release I'll be sharing with you some non-tutorialized fundamentals about the game to navigate it a bit better at first. I have a no-spoon-feeding policy about it so there are things you'll have to figure out on your own and lose -a lot- in the process.
